No margin notes. A Greek line and a German black-letter line sit inside the roman text. Signature mark at bottom right.

p.i: li in uxorem. Facite nobiscum affinitatem, & date nobis filias vestras, & filias nostras accipite vobis. Habitabitisq; apud nos, & terra ipsa erit coram vobis: habitate & negotiamini in ea, & possidete in ea. Sichem vero dixit ad patrem illius, & ad fratres eius: Inveniam gratiam in oculis vestris, & quicquid dixeritis ad me, dabo. Augete etiam plurimum super me dotem & munus, & dabo iuxta quod dixeritis mihi, modo detis mihi puellam in uxorem, &c.

main_text.p: 1 Ut facilius comprehendamus historiam in hoc capite contentam, distribuemus eam in tres partes: quarum prima fit de Dina filia Iacobi & Liæ. Hanc enim legimus egressam fuisse, nempe de tabernaculo seu domo patris sui, temerè & non consultis parentibus, ut videret mulieres regionis illius, & earum mores quales essent, perdifceret:item copressam esse à Sichem filio Emor:id quod nobis præscriptum est in doctrinam & admonitionem, 1. Corinth. 10. Rom. 15. Discant igitur puellæ occasiones peccatorum vitare, ac domi se potius continere, quàm extra paternas ædes (cum filio prodigo, Luc. 15.) hinc inde vagari: nam ut grauissimè Electra apud Euripidem inquit: [illegible, ~25 letters] Dann außgeben war nie so gut/ innen bleiben war besser,&c. non curiosæ esse,fi-

page.notes: The Greek line after "inquit:" is set in Greek type. I could not read its letters reliably at this scan resolution, so it is marked illegible rather than guessed. The German black-letter words are marked as best read: "außgeben", "innen" and "besser" are plausible readings, not certain. "perdifceret" is doubtful (possibly "perdiscceret"). "copressam" is copied as it appears. The italic opening is a quotation from the Vulgate (Genesis 34), copied as printed. A small stray bracket mark stands at the right edge near the top of the text; it is not printed text and is left out. The page ends with a hyphenated line ("fi-") and has no catchword.
